title: Trust boundaries and fail modes
summary: Which code decides at each step of a tool call, what happens when chock's hook does not run, and the gaps no hook covers.
intro: A tool call crosses several owners. The model proposes it, the vendor's client decides whether to run chock's hook and whether to honour its answer, chock's hook process judges it and writes a local log line, and git hooks and the CI gate check the change again at commit and on the pull request. The bottom group lists gaps the chock and agentseam docs state themselves.

boundaries.label: Your machine: the agent's client (vendor code)
Your machine: chock's processes, started by the client

nodes.label: Model and agent
nodes.card: The assurance case treats the agent session as an untrusted executor: it may ignore, misread or try to change its guidance. Its tool calls reach chock only when its client runs chock's hook.

nodes.label: Agent's client
nodes.card: Vendor code, not chock's. It decides whether to run the registered hook and whether to honour the Decision it returns, and what happens to the call when the hook crashes, times out or never starts. agentseam derives each agent's tier and fail mode from its matrix; the list below is that table.

nodes.label: Hook launcher
nodes.card: Every agent hook chock writes runs this script through git from the repository's top level. It starts the first Python 3.11+ that actually runs; with none it exits 2 and says why, and never allows.

nodes.label: Vendored runtime
nodes.card: One stdlib-only file per agent, generated by agentseam's bundler, with chock's handler inside. It parses the client's payload, runs the guard or gate, and answers in the client's dialect. If the handler raises, the bundled dispatcher refuses rather than allows.

nodes.label: Guard and gate
nodes.card: Runs a policy's guard script against the command. A guard that crashes or hits its timeout asks, a guard missing from disk denies, and only an empty command is allowed. Every check in one hook call shares the 30 s budget in gate/budget.py.

nodes.label: MCP gateway
nodes.card: Optional. chock gateway run is a stdio proxy the client launches in place of one MCP server, and refuses tools/call payloads that match a compiled gateway gate. Only MCP-routed calls cross it; the agent's native shell and file tools never do.

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.card: One line per runtime hook call, in .chock/log/gate-events.jsonl on the repo route or ~/.chock/log/<agent>/events.jsonl on the plugin route. It never raises, never changes the decision and never logs contents.

nodes.label: Git hooks
nodes.card: chock sync installs dispatchers in .git/hooks for pre-commit, pre-merge-commit and pre-push. Each runs the compiled gates through .chock/bin/gate.py, whichever agent or person made the commit.

nodes.label: CI gate
nodes.card: chock sync --ci writes .github/workflows/chock.yml, which re-runs the compiled gates over a pull request's commit range on a GitHub runner, where a local --no-verify does not reach. Until that workflow exists the surface enforces nothing and the coverage report does not credit it.

nodes.label: No hook surface
nodes.card: Some agents in agentseam's tier table have tier none or unadapted. tier_table.unadapted() lists them as agents a consumer can only reach by instruction files, so no pre-tool hook sees their calls.

nodes.label: Hook that dies
nodes.card: What the client does when chock's hook never runs or dies outright is the client's choice; the client box lists each agent's fail mode. chock's own 30 s budget per hook call is set below the 45 s timeout it writes into each client's hook config that takes one, so its own limits answer first.

nodes.label: Skipped git hooks
nodes.card: git commit --no-verify skips every git hook; for a human at a terminal, or on agents without hooks, nothing stops it. .git/hooks is not cloned, so a fresh clone enforces nothing until someone runs chock sync. chock check detects a disabled, deleted or tampered gate; it does not prevent one.

nodes.label: Guard evasion
nodes.card: Guards are best-effort pattern filters, not a security boundary. Quoting tricks, aliases and novel encodings can evade them.

nodes.label: Intent in content
nodes.card: For prompt injection in repo content, only invisible and direction-override Unicode is gated, at commit. The broader class of instructions hidden in content is advisory: no deterministic gate can read intent.

nodes.label: Branch protection
nodes.card: The CI workflow file is tracked content a pull request can delete. The CI gate holds only once it is a required status check, a server-side branch-protection setting nothing in the repository can edit.
